title: Score test as a named slope-at-the-null test
dek: Wikipedia score/Lagrange-multiplier test: use the reduced model's slope. Complementary to stats-wald-score.
story: The score test on Wikipedia uses the gradient of the log-likelihood at the restricted estimate, scaled by Fisher information. You fit only the reduced model. That is why GWAS likes score tests: one null GLM, many SNPs.
stats-wald-score already compares the trinity. This card is the encyclopedia score node, with the TB-lab reminder that rare events and separation make Wald explode while score stays defined.
Under Wilks regularity the three tests are first-order equivalent. Finite samples they are not the same object.
deep: Score statistic Sᵀ I⁻¹ S at θ̃₀.
Robust/sandwich scores exist when I is the wrong curvature (stats-sandwich).
Boundary issues still apply; a score at σ²=0 is not automatically χ²_1.
Do not mix a score p-value with a Bayes factor in one caption.

visual.caption: Score looks only at the reduced-model slope. Wald looks at the full-model estimate. LRT looks at both peaks. Three costumes, one nested question.
